preamble: Backing of the velar fricative [x] to the uvular fricative [χ] happens next to open or back vowels and as a general regional realization. Northern Dutch realizes its merged velar fricatives as [χ]. In Standard German, the ach-Laut is uvular [χ] after /a, aː/ but velar after /uː, oː/. Peninsular Spanish /x/ (jota) is post-velar or uvular in northern and central Spain, especially before /o, u/.

examples.note: In the north /ɣ/ is often realized the same as /x/, and the merged sound is described as post-velar [x̠] or uvular [χ] (also geeuw 'yawn' [χeːu]).
The ach-Laut is uvular [χ] after /a, aː/ but velar [x] after /uː, oː/ (Buch [buːx] 'book'); after /ʊ, ɔ, aʊ̯/ either occurs, [χ] more commonly.
In northern and central Spain /x/ is post-velar or uvular, at least before /o, u/; the preceding nasal assimilates to uvular [ɴ].
